target.statement: Shadow-FT (LoRA, r=128) tuned on BAAI-2k raises the Math-7 average of Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct to 27.2, versus 25.3 for conventional LoRA FT and 23.8 for the vanilla INSTRUCT baseline.
target.table_ref: Table 1 (row: Llama-3.2-1B; column: Avg./Math-7 under Full & LoRA)
target.dataset: BAAI-2k (2000 samples subsampled from BAAI/Infinity-Instruct, Gen split)

compute.basis: Training two LoRA runs (base + instruct) on a 1B model over 2k samples is small, but the target cell is a 7-benchmark generation average (AIME24, GSM8K 0-/8-shot, MATH, MATH-500, Minerva_Math, SVAMP) that the paper averages over three independent training runs, so CPU token generation dominates the wall-clock time.

blockers: The published protocol uses 8xA100 GPUs and reports means over 3 independent training runs; a single laptop run is a weakened reproduction.
Evaluation is done via OpenCompass + lmdeploy, and lmdeploy is CUDA-serving oriented, so a CPU evaluator would have to be rebuilt around transformers/vLLM-CPU.
Gated model licenses (Meta Llama 3.2/3.1) require HF account approval even though weights are free.
The BAAI-2k subset selection (high-reward filtering + uniform category sampling) must be re-derived from Infinity-Instruct/Gen, which may not exactly match the paper's 2k.
No paired BASE model exists for some LLMs (acknowledged in Limitations), though it does exist for the chosen Llama-3.2-1B target.
title: Shadow-FT: Tuning Instruct Model via Training on Paired Base Model
